name: Michele R. Jenkins
body:
Michele Jenkins sat on the board of the Santa Clarita Community College District, which runs College of the Canyons, for nearly forty years, until her death in February 2023.[1][2] She had been a student at the college in its first semester, in the fall of 1969, when its classes met in the evenings at Hart High School.[3][2] In 2015 the college called her the longest continuously serving member of its board.[3]

The district's accounts date her first election to 1984, and a college release of September 2004 said that by that December she would have served on the board for twenty years; the district's board history first lists her on the board of 1986-1987.[4][5][6]

She was the board's president in 1988, when it hired Dianne G. Van Hook to lead the college, and the college credits her with leading that search.[7][3] The college counted her presidency for 2014 as her eighth; The Signal, from figures the college supplied in 2023, gave her six terms as president, five as vice president and seven as clerk.[8][9]

She held Seat No. 2 while the trustees were elected at large: unopposed in 1995, re-elected in 2003 with 6,156 votes over Gordon Frank Richiusa and Michael Erwin, and unopposed in 2011.[10] After the district moved to trustee areas she won Trustee Area 4 in 2016 with 10,396 votes to Jerry Danielsen's 8,276, and again in 2020 with 13,306 to his 13,103.[10]

She sat on the board of the California Community College Trustees from 1994 to 2005, by the district's biography of her, and in September 2004, while president of that board, became president of the Community College League of California.[4][5] In 2015 the League gave her its "Fulfilling the Trust" award for her years of service.[3] The same biography lists an associate degree from the college, a bachelor's degree in anthropology from UCLA and a master's in counseling from the University of North Dakota, and gives her work as managing a family medical practice.[4]

She died on February 6, 2023, while a trustee, and on March 22 the board appointed Jerry Danielsen to her seat.[2][1] That month the board named the college's softball team room for her, and in January 2024 the college's foundation created the Michele R. Jenkins Leadership Endowment.[11][12]
footnotes: College of the Canyons, "Trustees Appoint Danielsen to Board," news release NR-03-28-23-board, March 28, 2023, canyons.edu/administration/pio/newsroom/2023-03-28-board.php: "The vacancy was created by the recent death of Michele Jenkins, who served as a board member for nearly 40 years"; "appointed Jerry Danielsen to fill Board Seat No. 4, effective immediately, at its March 22 meeting."

"Michele Jenkins, Longtime COC Trustee, Dies at 72," press release, SCVNews.com, February 10, 2023: "a member of the Santa Clarita Valley Community College District Board of Trustees that oversees College of the Canyons, died Monday, Feb. 6"; "Jenkins had served on the board as a trustee since 1984"; "Jenkins was enrolled as a student when the college opened for its first semester in fall 1969 at the Hart High School campus."

College of the Canyons, "COC Grad Jenkins Honored for 3 Decades of Board Service," SCVNews.com, June 30, 2015: "Forty-six years after enrolling in the first classes offered by College of the Canyons, held in the evenings at Hart High School"; "First elected in 1984, she currently is the longest continuously serving member of the board"; "Jenkins received the CCLC's 'Fulfilling the Trust' service award"; "hiring Dr. Van Hook to lead the college in 1988. Jenkins was president of the board then".

Santa Clarita Community College District, Board of Trustees, "Member Profiles," canyons.edu/administration/board/profiles.php, as captured by the Internet Archive on October 1, 2020 (web.archive.org/web/20201001223223/https://www.canyons.edu/administration/board/profiles.php): under "Ms. Michele R. Jenkins": "President"; "Elected Board Member since 1984"; "Manages three-physician family medical practice"; "A.A., College of the Canyons"; "B.A., Anthropology, UCLA"; "M.A., Counseling, University of North Dakota"; "Member, California Community College Trustees (CCCT) Board of Directors, 1994-2005"; "President, CCCT Board and CCLC Board, 2004-2005". The capture of February 2, 2023 reads "Elected in 1984".

College of the Canyons, "Jenkins Assumes Statewide Community College Leadership Position," news release, September 28, 2004, canyons.edu/info/news/nr092804-jenkins.html, as captured by the Internet Archive on October 25, 2004: "has assumed the position of president of the Community College League of California"; "This December she will have served on the COC board for 20 years. In addition, Jenkins has served on the California Community College Trustee Board (elected by all of the district trustees in the state) for 9.5 years and currently serves as president."

Santa Clarita Community College District, Board of Trustees, "History," canyons.edu/administration/board/history.php, as of October 5, 2026: the board of 1984-1985 lists four names, "Linda C. Cubbage, President", "Donald M. Benton, VP", "Richard G. Peoples" and "Mark A. Posner"; that of 1986-1987 adds "Michele R. Jenkins"; that of 1988-1989 begins "Michele R. Jenkins, President".

College of the Canyons, "Dr. Dianne G. Van Hook: 25 Years at the Helm of COC," July 1, 2013, as carried on SCVHistory.com, /scvhistory/dvh070113.htm: "A member of the Board of Trustees today and in 1988, Jenkins was the board president who led the development of the CEO search."

College of the Canyons, "Jenkins Takes Helm of COC Board for 8th Time," SCVNews.com, December 10, 2013: "Jenkins, who also served as board president in 1988 when the college hired COC Chancellor Dr. Dianne G. Van Hook, will be serving her eighth term as board president." The district's board history lists her as president for 1988-1989, 1991, 1996, 2001, 2007, 2011, 2014-2015 and 2020.

Perry Smith, "Longtime COC board member dies at age 72," The Signal, February 10, 2023, signalscv.com/2023/02/longtime-coc-board-member-dies-at-age-72/: "Michele Jenkins served six terms as board president, five as vice president and seven as board clerk, according to information provided by COC."

Archive records: the Santa Clarita Community College District board elections of November 7, 1995, November 4, 2003, November 8, 2011, November 8, 2016 and November 3, 2020, with their returns; California Elections Data Archive (CEDA), a compilation of the County's returns (CEDA1995Data.xls, row 1365, Seat 2, 6,223 of 6,223; CEDA2003Data.xls, row 1367; CEDA2011Data.xlsx, row 1231, 10,895 of 10,895; CEDA2016Data.xlsx, rows 3806-3807; CEDA2020Data.xlsx, row 6252).

College of the Canyons, "COC Athletic Facilities Named to Honor Smelser, Gillespie, Jenkins," SCVNews.com, March 9, 2023: "All three projects were approved at the board's meeting on Wednesday, March 8"; "Naming of the softball team room to 'Michele Jenkins Team Room'".

College of the Canyons, "COC Foundation Creates Endowment Honoring Michele Jenkins," SCVNews.com, January 4, 2024: "The Michele R. Jenkins Leadership Endowment will support Bridging the Canyons, the Michele R. Jenkins Scholarship and faculty development at the college."
notesForNathan: When her service began: 1984 in the district's biographies (2020, 2023), the college's releases of 2015 and 2023 and The Signal's obituary, and December 1984 by the release of September 2004; the district's board history first lists her for 1986-1987, and its 1984-1985 board has only four names. Footnoted both; the text states neither. If you accept 1984, the holding can start 1984-12.

How many times president: "eighth term" for 2014 (college, 2013) against "six terms" (The Signal 2023, from COC figures); the board history lists her as president for eight years or spans (1988-1989, 1991, 1996, 2001, 2007, 2011, 2014-2015, 2020). Footnoted both; the text gives no total of its own.
The SCVNews obituary (February 10, 2023) says she "was last re-elected to the board in 2021"; the returns and the college's release of December 2020 put it on November 3, 2020. Not used.

Left out as private: her husband, children and parents, her birth date and place (in the endowment release), her age at death, and the Outstanding Alumni Award she shared with her husband. The Signal (MacGregor, quoted) credits her with helping found the valley's League of Women Voters chapter and AAUW branch; second-hand and not used.
No Wikipedia used.

name: John D. Hoskinson
body: John D. Hoskinson sat on the board of the Santa Clarita Community College District in 1988-1989 and again in 1997, when he was its clerk, by the district's board history, which does not say how either period began or ended.[1] In the election of November 4, 1997, standing for Seat No. 1 with the ballot designation "Appointed Incumbent," he came third of three, with 1,590 votes, behind Ernie Tichenor and Richard G. Peoples.[2] That return is the one record from his years on the board cited here; the rest comes from the district's later list.[2][1]
footnotes: Santa Clarita Community College District, Board of Trustees, "History," canyons.edu/administration/board/history.php, as of October 5, 2026: "John D. Hoskinson" on the board of 1988-1989; "John Hoskinson, Clerk" on the board of 1997. He is not on the boards of 1990 to 1996 or of 1998.

Archive record: the Santa Clarita Community College District board election of November 4, 1997, with its returns; California Elections Data Archive (CEDA), a compilation of the County's returns, CEDA1997Data.xls, rows 1411-1413: Seat 1, "John D. Hoskinson" 1,590, ballot designation "Appointed Incumbent"; Richard G. Peoples 1,716; Ernie Tichenor 3,832, elected.
notesForNathan: Retrospective: one lifetime source (the 1997 return). How he came to the board in the 1980s, when he left, and when he was appointed before 1997 (and to whose seat) are not found.

Probable, not stated: the John Hoskinson who was SCV Man of the Year 1999 (mwoty.htm), the COC Foundation's Silver Spur honoree of 1994 (silverspur-list.htm), one of the City founders on the plaque in the City's 20th-anniversary book (sc19872007, flipbook p. 11), and the "John D. Hoskinson" of Gruber Systems (33 years, chairman and CEO from 2006) who became director of the college's Small Business Development Center in March 2015 (SCVNews, February 27 and May 12, 2015; saved). No source read names him as the former trustee. If you accept the identity, those give a fuller public-life profile.

Not used: a federal Department of Labor complaint of May 2015 against Gruber Systems and its former CEO, John Hoskinson, over the company's employee stock plan (Perry Smith, KHTS via SCVNews, June 4, 2015; saved). It concerns the Gruber man, the identity is not settled, and the outcome was not read. Yours to decide if the identity is accepted.
researchLeads: A John D. Hoskinson of Gruber Systems became director of the college's Small Business Development Center in 2015, and a John Hoskinson was the valley's Man of the Year in 1999, the College of the Canyons Foundation's Silver Spur honoree in 1994, and one of the City founders on the plaque in the City's 20th-anniversary book. No source names any of them as the former trustee, so none is stated here. (5 October 2026, the college trustee drafts.)

name: Ernest Moreno
body: Ernest Moreno sat on the board of the Santa Clarita Community College District from 1990 to 1995, by the district's board history, which lists him as its clerk in 1992, vice president in 1993 and president in 1994.[1] Carl Boyer, who was mayor of Santa Clarita in 1991, wrote in his history of the city that Moreno was serving on the college board in 1991, in a passage on the growth of the valley's Hispanic population.[2] What is known here of his service comes from these two later accounts, and neither says how it began or ended.[1][2]
footnotes: Santa Clarita Community College District, Board of Trustees, "History," canyons.edu/administration/board/history.php, as of October 5, 2026: "Ernest Moreno" on the boards of 1990 and 1991; "Ernest Moreno, Clerk" in 1992; "Ernest Moreno, VP" in 1993; "Ernest Moreno, President" in 1994; "Ernest Moreno" in 1995. He is not on the board of 1996.

Carl Boyer 3rd, Santa Clarita: The Formation and Organization of the Largest Newly Incorporated City in the History of Humankind, 2nd ed. (2015), chapter 14, "First Term as Mayor," p. 204, as carried on SCVHistory.com, /scvhistory/files/boyer2015ch14/: "The growth in the Hispanic population was significant. Ernest Moreno was serving on the Santa Clarita Community College District governing board in 1991, and Gloria Mercado served on the William S. Hart Union High School District board from 1997 to 2001."
notesForNathan: Retrospective: no source from his years on the board was found. The board history and Boyer (2015) are later accounts; Boyer was mayor at the time, so the 1991 statement is a participant's recollection.

How he came to the board (election of 1989? appointment?) and how he left (1995 election, in which no Moreno stood, per CEDA) are not found. CEDA's college rows begin in 1995. The archive holds no candidacy for him.

Searched for him: the mirror (Python, cp1252) for "Ernest Moreno", "Ernie Moreno" and "Moreno" in every COC, Canyon Call and Boyer file; SCVNews search ("Ernie Moreno": no results). A "Leonard Ernest Moreno Sr." obituary (1961-2015) on the mirror is a different man by dates and name.

name: Joan W. MacGregor
body:
Joan MacGregor sat on the board of the Santa Clarita Community College District, which runs College of the Canyons, for 31 years, from her election in 1993 until she resigned in August 2024; before that she had been a trustee of the Sulphur Springs Union School District.[1][2][3] The district's biography of her gives her twenty years on the Sulphur Springs board, and lists her as founder of the Santa Clarita Valley Trustees Association, a past PTA president and president of the valley's PTA Council.[4]

Carl Boyer, in his account of his first term as mayor, which began in December 1990, describes her as president of the Sulphur Springs board, criticizing Councilwoman Jan Heidt after the City Council sent back for revision the district's plan to build a shopping center on the site of an old school to pay for a new one.[5] In 2012 she was on the campaign committee for Measure CK, a Sulphur Springs school bond.[6]

On the college board she held Seat No. 3 while the trustees were elected at large: unopposed in 1997, and re-elected in 2001 over William J. Broyles, in 2005 over Theresa Todd and Ronald A. Vitale, by 16,751 votes to 15,621 and 3,024, and in 2009 over Randy R. Moberg.[7][8] In 2013 she was the only candidate for her seat and was appointed in lieu of election.[9] After the district moved to trustee areas she won Trustee Area 5 in 2018 over Ann-Marie Bjorkman, 7,229 votes to 5,882, and in 2022 she ran unopposed.[7][1]

Her candidate statement of 2005 gave her occupation as owner of Valley Oaks Properties and named her a past education director of the California Association of Realtors; the district's biography calls her vice president of Valley Oaks Properties, a real estate brokerage.[10][4] The biography calls her a three-time president of the board; its board history lists her as president in 1997, 2002, 2005 and 2009.[4][11] She sat on the Canyon Country Site Selection Advisory Committee, by the same biography, and in 2024 she named the opening of the Canyon Country campus in 2007 among the things she was proudest of.[4][2] In December 2022 the college called her the longest-serving local public official.[1]

She announced in April 2024 that she would leave before her term ended in 2026, and her resignation took effect on August 5, 2024.[2][3] Because she did not resign in time for a special election to be held with the November election, the board filled the seat by appointment, and she said at one of her last meetings, as The Signal reported, that she had timed it so on purpose, because more people apply for an appointment than run for a seat.[12][13] The board appointed Carlos Guerrero to the seat on September 18, 2024.[14]
footnotes: College of the Canyons, "Board of Trustees Names New Officers," news release NR-12-22-22-board, December 22, 2022, canyons.edu/administration/pio/newsroom/2022-12-22-board.php: "Joan MacGregor, the longest-serving local public official, having served on the Sulphur Springs School District board prior to her election to the COC board in 1993, ran unopposed in November and was sworn in to represent Trustee Area 5."

Tyler Wainfeld, "COC board member announces intent to step down," The Signal, April 25, 2024, signalscv.com/2024/04/coc-board-member-announces-intent-to-step-down/: "After 51 years as a local school board member, Joan MacGregor announced at Wednesday's Santa Clarita Community College District board of trustees meeting that she is planning to step down"; "she will not carry out the final two and a half years of her term"; "Previously a member of the Sulphur Springs Union School District governing board for 20 years before spending the past 31 years as a trustee of the SCCCD"; "one of the things she is most proud of was the opening of the COC Canyon Country campus in 2007".

College of the Canyons, "Aug. 14: COC Trustees to Consider Timeline to Fill Second Open Board Seat," SCVNews.com, August 11, 2024: "The resignation of Trustee Joan W. MacGregor effective Aug. 5 has resulted in a vacant board seat in Area 5."

Santa Clarita Community College District, Board of Trustees, "Member Profiles," canyons.edu/administration/board/profiles.php, as captured by the Internet Archive on February 25, 2024 (web.archive.org/web/20240225144905/https://www.canyons.edu/administration/board/profiles.php): under "Ms. Joan W. MacGregor": "Elected in 1993"; "Three-time president of Board of Trustees"; "Member, Canyon Country Site Selection Advisory Committee"; "Vice president, Valley Oaks Properties Inc. real estate brokerage (retired)"; "Past trustee, Sulphur Springs Union School District (20 years)"; "Founder of SCV Trustees Association; PTA president, SCV PTA Council president". The capture of October 1, 2020 reads the same, without "(retired)".

Carl Boyer 3rd, Santa Clarita: The Formation and Organization of the Largest Newly Incorporated City in the History of Humankind, 2nd ed. (2015), chapter 14, "First Term as Mayor," p. 211, as carried on SCVHistory.com, /scvhistory/files/boyer2015ch14/: "Jan Heidt was the subject of intense criticism by Joan MacGregor, then president of the Sulphur Springs Union School District. The school district was in the process of closing an old school and building a shopping center on the land to provide funds for a new school. Jan voiced concern about traffic and aesthetic issues, and the council voted four to one (McKeon dissenting) to send the plans back for revisions." The chapter opens with his swearing-in as mayor on December 11, 1990.

SCV Newsmaker of the Week, "Joan MacGregor & Shelley Weinstein, Sulphur Springs School Bond Measure CK," SCVTV, May 1, 2012, scvtv.com/html/notw333.html: "Joan MacGregor is a College of the Canyons trusteee and former member of the Sulphur Springs School Board"; "Both are members of the Measure CK campaign committee."

Archive records: the Santa Clarita Community College District board elections of November 4, 1997, November 6, 2001, November 8, 2005, November 3, 2009 and November 6, 2018, with their returns; California Elections Data Archive (CEDA), a compilation of the County's returns (CEDA1997Data.xls, row 1417, Seat 3, 4,980 of 4,980; CEDA2001Data.xls, row 1576, 9,815 to Broyles's 7,388; CEDA2005Data.xls, row 1752; CEDA2009Data.xls, row 1547, 8,629 to Moberg's 4,830, where the name is printed "John Whaling MacGregor"; CEDA2018Data.xlsx, row 4906).

Smart Voter (League of Women Voters of California Education Fund), "Governing Board Member; Santa Clarita Community College District; Office No. 3," November 8, 2005, smartvoter.org/2005/11/08/ca/la/race/110/, as captured by the Internet Archive: "Joan Whaling Mac Gregor 16,751 votes 47.32%"; "Teresa Todd 15,621 votes 44.13%". Smart Voter's page for 2009, Office 3, prints her name "Joan Whaling MacGregor", 8,629 votes.

County of Los Angeles, Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk, Consolidated Elections, November 5, 2013, Final List of Qualified Candidates Whose Name Will Not Appear on the Ballot: under "SANTA CLARITA COMMUNITY COLLEGE DISTRICT" and "Governing Board Member, Seat No. 3", "*JOAN WHALING MAC GREGOR", "Incumbent", the only candidate ("Total Candidates for Contest: 1").

Smart Voter, "Joan Whaling Mac Gregor," candidate page, November 8, 2005 election, smartvoter.org/2005/11/08/ca/la/vote/macgregor_j/, as captured by the Internet Archive; information "provided by the candidate": "Incumbent/12 years Santa Clarita College Board of Trustees"; "Trustee 20 years Sulphur Springs School District"; "Owner Valley Oaks Properties"; "Past Education Director Califormia Association of Realtors" [sic].

Santa Clarita Community College District, Board of Trustees, "History," canyons.edu/administration/board/history.php, as of October 5, 2026: "Joan W. MacGregor, President" on the boards of 1997, 2002, 2005 and 2009.

Tyler Wainfeld, "L.A. City College professor selected as new COC board member," The Signal, September 19, 2024, signalscv.com/2024/09/valley-college-professor-selected-as-new-coc-board-member/: "An appointment process was chosen by the board due to the fact that MacGregor did not resign in time for a special election to be consolidated with the upcoming general election. MacGregor told the crowd in attendance at one of her last meetings that she had intentionally done that because, from her experience, more people are inclined to apply for a seat rather than campaign for one."

Tyler Wainfeld, "New COC board members take their places," The Signal, December 19, 2024, signalscv.com/2024/12/new-coc-board-members-take-their-places/: "MacGregor said at one of her last meetings that she intentionally did not resign until after the deadline to consolidate a special election with the Nov. 5 general election".

College of the Canyons, "Board of Trustees Appoints Carlos Guerrero," news release NR-09-19-24-BOT, September 19, 2024, canyons.edu/administration/pio/newsroom/2024-09-19-bot.php: "appointed Carlos Guerrero to fill Board Seat No. 5, effective immediately, at its September 18 meeting. The vacancy was created by the recent resignation of Joan MacGregor, who served as a board member for 31 years."
notesForNathan: Presidencies: the district's biography and The Signal (April 2024) say three; the district's board history lists four (1997, 2002, 2005, 2009). Footnoted both; the text states neither as fact.

The 1993 election return is not held (CEDA's college rows begin in 1995). The 2022 contest was cancelled (County list names Areas 1 and 5); that she was the Area 5 appointee rests on the college's "ran unopposed" (December 2022), not a County appointee list.

Sulphur Springs years: "20 years" (biography, her 2005 statement, The Signal 2024). The Signal's "51 years as a local school board member" implies about 1973 to 1993; not stated. No Sulphur Springs candidacy or holding exists in the archive. A holding for her Sulphur Springs service could be proposed if you want one.

Spelling: the archive's 2005 candidacy and CEDA print "Theresa Todd"; Smart Voter prints "Teresa Todd". The text follows the archive's record. CEDA 2009's "John Whaling MacGregor" is a misprint, confirmed by Smart Voter's 2009 race page (saved).

Not used: The Signal's editorial of July 13, 2024 ("MacGregor Thumbs Her Nose at Voters", saved), which is opinion, and the board's July 2024 decision to place Chancellor Van Hook on leave, in which the editorial says she took part; no news report of that vote was read. Boyer's 1991 anecdote is kept as his account; cut it if you think it too slight.

Left out as private: her residence and the address, telephone and email in the County's 2013 list and her 2005 Smart Voter page (redacted in the saved copy); her great-grandchildren (The Signal, April 2024); the 1984 friendship with Jenkins.

name: Ronald E. Gillis
body:
Ron Gillis, a plumber by his ballot designation of 1995, was elected to Seat No. 5 on the board of the Santa Clarita Community College District on November 7, 1995, defeating the incumbent, Richard G. Peoples, 4,429 votes to 3,118.[1] He was re-elected on November 4, 2003, with 4,719 votes, over Rick Winsman and Sheldon S. Wigdor.[1][2] The district's board history lists him from 1996 to 2006, as its vice president in 1998 and 2004, president in 1999, and clerk in 2002 and 2003.[3] He and Joan MacGregor appeared as College of the Canyons trustees on the hundredth episode of SCV Newsmaker of the Week.[4]

He left the seat in July 2006, by the college's announcement of his successor, and on August 23, 2006 the board chose Scott Wilk to fill it.[5]
footnotes: Archive records: the Santa Clarita Community College District board elections of November 7, 1995 and November 4, 2003, with their returns; California Elections Data Archive (CEDA), a compilation of the County's returns: CEDA1995Data.xls, row 1367, Seat 5, "Ron Gillis" 4,429, ballot designation "Plumber", and Richard G. Peoples 3,118, "Incumbent"; CEDA2003Data.xls, row 1385, Seat 5, "Ron Gillis" 4,719, "Incumbent".

Smart Voter (League of Women Voters of California Education Fund), "Governing Board Member; Santa Clarita Community College District; Office 5," November 4, 2003, smartvoter.org/2003/11/04/ca/la/race/01526000/, as captured by the Internet Archive: "Ron Gillis 4,719 votes 52.85% Occupation: Incumbent"; "Rick Winsman 3,146 votes 35.23%"; "Sheldon S. Wigdor 1,064 votes 11.92%".

Santa Clarita Community College District, Board of Trustees, "History," canyons.edu/administration/board/history.php, as of October 5, 2026: "Ronald E. Gillis" on the boards of 1996 to 2006; "Ronald E. Gillis, VP" in 1998 and 2004; "Ronald E. Gillis, President" in 1999; "Ronald E. Gillis, Clerk" in 2002 and 2003. He is not on the board of 2007.
SCV Newsmaker of the Week, list of episodes, SCVHistory.com, /scvhistory/signal/newsmaker/index.htm: "Episode 100 | Joan MacGregor & Ron Gillis, COC Trustees". The episode is not dated in the list.

College of the Canyons, "Board of Trustees Appoints Scott Wilk to Vacant Seat," news release No. COC-07-019, August 25, 2006, canyons.edu/offices/pio/nr082506wilk.html, as captured by the Internet Archive on September 14, 2006: "Wilk was one of 20 community candidates interviewed by the board during open session on Aug. 23"; "Wilk ... will serve in his position until the seat, vacated by Ron Gillis in July, comes up for re-election in November 2007."
notesForNathan: His 1999 re-election (if contested) is not in CEDA (no college rows for 1999) and no return is held; the board history's unbroken listing implies he served on, which the text leaves unsaid.
Why he left in July 2006 (resigned? moved?) is not found; the release says only "vacated".

Not used: The Signal's obituary of his wife, Roberta Gillis (April 15, 2006, sg041506-gillis.htm), a family matter. The Newsmaker episode page (sg082805-nm.htm) is not on the mirror and the Internet Archive refused the request; its date is not stated.
Lifetime sources: the 1995 and 2003 returns, Smart Voter 2003, the 2006 release and the Newsmaker list; the board history is later. Short form.

name: Ernest L. Tichenor
body:
Ernie Tichenor, whose ballot designation in 1997 was "Attorney/Educator," was elected to Seat No. 1 on the board of the Santa Clarita Community College District on November 4, 1997, with 3,832 votes, defeating the appointed incumbent, John D. Hoskinson, and Richard G. Peoples.[1] He was re-elected unopposed in 2001, and in 2005 by 18,686 votes to 18,091 for Jonathan D. Kraut.[1][2] The district's board history lists him from 1998 to 2008, as its president in 2000, 2004 and 2008.[3] When Michael D. Berger was elected to Seat No. 1 in November 2009, Tichenor was not among the candidates.[1]

In August 2011, by then living in Fairfax County, Virginia, Tichenor was arrested on a charge of soliciting a minor over the Internet, as Leon Worden reported in SCVNews.[4] He pleaded guilty on July 27, 2012 to one felony count of using "a communications system to facilitate certain offenses with a child," and was found dead on November 9, 2012, the morning he was due to be sentenced.[5]
footnotes: Archive records: the Santa Clarita Community College District board elections of November 4, 1997, November 6, 2001, November 8, 2005 and November 3, 2009, with their returns; California Elections Data Archive (CEDA), a compilation of the County's returns: CEDA1997Data.xls, row 1413, Seat 1, "Ernie Tichenor" 3,832, ballot designation "Attorney/Educator", with John D. Hoskinson, "Appointed Incumbent", 1,590, and Richard G. Peoples 1,716; CEDA2001Data.xls, row 1560, 15,410 of 15,410; CEDA2005Data.xls, row 1740, 18,686 to Jonathan Kraut's 18,091; CEDA2009Data.xls, Seat 1: Michael David Berger, Robin L. Bryce, John L. Dortch and Brian E. Koegle.

Smart Voter (League of Women Voters of California Education Fund), "Governing Board Member; Santa Clarita Community College District; Office No. 1," November 8, 2005, smartvoter.org/2005/11/08/ca/la/race/109/, as captured by the Internet Archive: "Ernie Tichenor 18,686 votes 50.81% Occupation: Incumbent"; "Jonathan D. Kraut 18,091 votes 49.19%".

Santa Clarita Community College District, Board of Trustees, "History," canyons.edu/administration/board/history.php, as of October 5, 2026: "Ernest L. name: Michael D. Berger
body:
Mike Berger was president of the Santa Clarita Valley Chamber of Commerce in 1989, sat on the City of Santa Clarita's Planning Commission for most of the years from 1994 to 2008, and was a trustee of the Santa Clarita Community College District from 2009 to 2022.[1][2][3][4]

Leon Worden's captions to two chamber photographs call him president-elect of the chamber in May 1988 and its president in September 1989, when he was with Shearson Lehman Hutton.[5][1] By Worden's account he served on the Planning Commission from 1994 to 2008 except for 1996 to 1998, and the City's list of commissioners agrees.[1][3] As a commissioner in 2005 he spoke for the Downtown Newhall specific plan, which the commission approved and sent to the City Council.[6]

He was elected to Seat No. 1 on the college board on November 3, 2009, first of four candidates with 6,581 votes, under the ballot designation "Finance Businessman."[7] In 2013 he was the only candidate for the seat and was appointed in lieu of election.[8] The board's history lists him as its president in 2012, 2013 and 2019.[9] He retired from the board in December 2022 after thirteen years, and Chuck Lyon succeeded him in Trustee Area 1.[4]

Before he joined the board he had served twenty years on the board of the College of the Canyons Foundation, which gave him its Silver Spur Award for Community Service in 2000, and he was named Santa Clarita Valley Man of the Year for 2006.[4][10][11][12] A former student of the college, he was a senior vice president of Morgan Stanley by 2016.[13]

name: Steven D. Zimmer
body:
Steve Zimmer headed the Newhall Ranch division of The Newhall Land and Farming Company from 1999, leading the planning and approval of the company's development west of Interstate 5, and was a trustee of the Santa Clarita Community College District from 2013 to 2020.[1][2]

A real estate lawyer, he came to Newhall Land in 1999 from the Oxnard firm of Rupp, Holmberg & Zimmer, and had earlier been city attorney of El Centro and chief assistant county counsel of Imperial County.[1][3] By Leon Worden's report of 2013 he was responsible for getting the Newhall Ranch specific plan approved by the county Board of Supervisors in 2003.[2] After eleven years with Newhall Land, which he left as executive vice president, he joined the law firm of Gilchrist & Rutter in October 2011.[3]

He joined the board of the College of the Canyons Foundation in 2002 and chaired it from 2004 to 2007.[4][5] On January 14, 2013 the college board chose him from thirteen applicants to fill the seat left by Scott Wilk, who had been elected to the Assembly.[2] Because an appointee could serve no more than eighteen months without an election, he filed for the seat that summer; as the only candidate he was appointed in lieu of election in 2013, and again in 2016 for Trustee Area 3.[5][6][7]

The board's history lists him as its clerk in 2014-2015, vice president in 2016 and president in 2017-2018.[8] He retired from the board in December 2020 after eight years, and Sebastian Cazares succeeded him.[4] By the district's biography he also chaired the board of directors of the Child and Family Center.[9]

name: Edel Alonso
body:
Edel Alonso was a counselor at Hart and Valencia high schools and then a counselor and professor at College of the Canyons from 1999 to 2015, and since 2016 she has represented Trustee Area 2 on the board of the Santa Clarita Community College District, which runs the college.[1][2]

At the college she was president of the Academic Senate and co-chair of the President's Advisory Committee on Budget, by the district's biography of her, which also lists degrees from Montclair State University, Loyola Marymount University and the University of La Verne, and her service as chair of the Civil Rights in Education Committee of the California Teachers Association's State Council.[2]

Standing as a retired college counselor, she won Trustee Area 2 on November 8, 2016 with 7,261 votes, defeating the incumbent, Bruce Fortine, and R. Baldwin-Kennedy.[3] She was re-elected in 2020 over Tony Watson, 14,061 votes to 9,788, and in 2024 over Scott Schauer, 11,403 to 11,266.[3] The board chose her as its clerk for 2020, its president for 2021 and each year through 2024, and its clerk again for 2026.[4][5][6][7]

In December 2024 her nomination for a fifth year as president failed, and the board elected Sharlene Johnson.[8]

name: Sebastian C. M. Cazares
body:
Sebastian Cazares, a graduate of Saugus High School and of College of the Canyons, where he was president of the Associated Student Government, represented Trustee Area 3 on the board of the Santa Clarita Community College District from 2020 to 2024.[1][2] Standing as an "Education/Student Advocate," he won the seat on November 3, 2020 with 13,608 votes to Fred Arnold's 12,572, succeeding Steve Zimmer.[3][4] He had served on the college's Independent Citizens Bond Oversight Committee, by the district's biography, and in December 2022 the college called him the youngest elected official in Los Angeles County.[1][5]

The board chose him as its clerk for 2022, its vice president for 2023, and its clerk again in August 2024.[2][6] He was one of the plaintiffs, with Michael Cruz and Neighborhood Elections Now, in the suit under the California Voting Rights Act that the City of Santa Clarita settled on April 12, 2022, after which the city moved to electing its council by district.[7] He did not stand for re-election in 2024, and Fred Arnold won the seat.[2][8]

name: Charles L. Lyon
body:
Chuck Lyon was a player, coach, athletic director and dean at College of the Canyons, twenty-three years on its staff in all, and from 2022 to 2024 he sat on the board of the Santa Clarita Community College District, which runs the college.[1][2]

As the college's quarterback in 1973-1974 he scored the first touchdown in Cougar Stadium, by the district's biography of him, and he was the quarterback of the team that won the conference title in 1975 under coach Larry Reisbig.[1][3] The college's student newspaper reported two touchdowns by him in the homecoming win over Moorpark in November 1974.[4]

After twelve years as a faculty member and coach at Pasadena City College, he came back to College of the Canyons in 1998 as a faculty member and head football coach; his team won the national and state community college championships in 2004, and he was named National Community College Football Coach of the Year.[2][1] In February 2004 he was featured, as the college's head football coach, on SCV Newsmaker of the Week.[5] He was the college's athletic director from 2007 to 2016 and its dean and athletic director from 2017.[2]

With the endorsement of the retiring trustee Mike Berger, he stood for Trustee Area 1 in 2022, ran unopposed, and took his seat in December.[6][2] The board chose him as its vice president for 2024.[7] He resigned effective June 27, 2024, without giving a reason; because he resigned in time, the seat went on the November ballot, and Darlene Trevino won it.[8][9][10]

name: Jerry K. Danielsen
body:
Jerry Danielsen, owner of Busy Signal Studios, a recording studio in Canyon Country, sat on the board of the Santa Clarita Community College District from March 2023 to December 2024, appointed to the seat left by the death of Michele Jenkins.[1][2]

He had stood twice before for Trustee Area 4 against Jenkins, as a "Small Business Owner," losing in 2016 by 8,276 votes to 10,396 and in 2020 by 13,103 to 13,306.[3] The board appointed him to Board Seat No. 4 on March 22, 2023.[1] It chose him as its clerk for 2024, and on July 1, 2024, after Chuck Lyon resigned, as its vice president.[4][5] In November 2024, standing as the appointed incumbent, he lost Trustee Area 4 to Sharlene Rose Johnson, 10,626 votes to 12,821.[3][2]

The college's announcement of his appointment calls him a College of the Canyons graduate of 1979, who studied at Sound Master Recording Engineering School in 1984 and earned a bachelor of fine arts degree in music composition from CalArts in 1992, and co-owner of Pantheon Media; it says he organized monthly educational events for the Los Angeles Section of the Audio Engineering Society.[1] The district's biography calls him an educator and small business owner, and a graduate of William S. Hart High School.[6]

name: Carlos R. Guerrero
body:
Carlos Guerrero, a professor of Chicano studies in the social science department of Los Angeles City College, was appointed to the board of the Santa Clarita Community College District on September 18, 2024, to fill the Trustee Area 5 seat left by Joan MacGregor's resignation, for the rest of a term that comes up for election on November 3, 2026.[1][2]

The board chose him over the one other applicant it interviewed, Tony Maldonado; a third applicant had withdrawn.[3] The College of the Canyons Faculty Association had endorsed him.[4] The district's biography lists him also as a lecturer in Chicana and Chicano studies at California State University, Northridge, with a doctorate in cultural studies from Claremont Graduate University.[2] In December 2025 he and Sharlene Johnson were the nominees for board president, and the vote deadlocked two to two.[5] On May 3, 2026 he was elected to the board of the California Community College Trustees for 2026-27.[6]

name: Fred Arnold
body:
Fred Arnold, a mortgage adviser who founded American Family Funding in Santa Clarita, was chairman of the Santa Clarita Valley Chamber of Commerce in 2013 and was elected to the board of the Santa Clarita Community College District for Trustee Area 3 in 2024.[1][2][3]

The chamber's announcement of his chairmanship, in April 2012, said he hosted the SCVTV program "Out of the Rough" and a KHTS radio program for chamber members.[1] He had been president of a state association of mortgage brokers, which the announcement calls the California Association of Mortgage Professionals and the district's biography the California Association of Mortgage Brokers.[1][4] In June 2012, as the chamber's chairman-elect, he appeared on SCV Newsmaker of the Week to speak about the valley's military veterans.[5]

He chaired the board of the College of the Canyons Foundation and the district's Independent Citizens Bond Oversight Committee, by the district's biography, and was chairing the foundation when he ran for the board in 2024.[4][6] He first stood for Trustee Area 3 in 2020, as a "Finance Business Advisor," and lost to Sebastian Cazares, 12,572 votes to 13,608.[3] In 2024, with Cazares not running, he won the seat with 12,271 votes, over Andrew "Andy" Taban and Tasha C. Hoggatt.[3][7] The board chose him as its vice president for 2025 and 2026.[8][9]

name: Sharlene Rose Johnson
body: Sharlene Johnson, a real estate agent, was elected to the board of the Santa Clarita Community College District for Trustee Area 4 on November 5, 2024, defeating the appointed incumbent, Jerry Danielsen, 12,821 votes to 10,626; her ballot designation was "Foundation Board Member."[1][2] The district's biography lists her as a member of the College of the Canyons Foundation's board, a past board president of JCI Santa Clarita Valley and president of the California Jaycees, and a member of the oversight committee for the William S. Hart Union High School District's bond Measure SA, and gives her an associate degree from the college and a bachelor's degree in business administration from California State University, Northridge.[2] The board chose her as its president for 2025, and again, after a deadlocked vote in December 2025, at its meeting of January 9, 2026.[3][4][5] Under her former name, Sharlene Rose Duzick, she had stood for the board of the Saugus Union School District in Trustee Area 5 in 2018 and 2022, and lost both times.[6][7]
